title: 👥 UNIT 4: POPULATION POLICIES, PROGRAMS AND THE ENVIRONMENT
notes: Population is a major factor in economic development, resource use and environmental conditions.

title: 📈 4.1 THEORIES ON POPULATION GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Population theories explain relationships between population growth, resources, food production, poverty and development.

Major perspectives → Malthusian → Neo-Malthusian → Marxian → Boserupian → Demographic Transition Theory.

title: 🌾 4.1.1 MALTHUSIAN THEORY
notes:
Thomas Robert Malthus argued that population tends to grow faster than food production.

👥 Population → grows geometrically.
🌾 Food production → grows arithmetically.

If unchecked → population pressure creates poverty, hunger and resource shortages.

🔹 Preventive checks → reduce births, including delayed marriage and moral restraint.
🔹 Positive checks → increase deaths through famine, disease, war and other disasters.

⭐ Main idea → population pressure is controlled by checks when it exceeds available subsistence.

title: ⚠️ 4.1.2 NEO-MALTHUSIAN VIEW
notes:
Neo-Malthusians retain the idea that rapid population growth can contribute to poverty and resource pressure.

🔹 Population growth → viewed as an important cause of resource and development problems.

🔹 Birth control → considered a way of limiting rapid population growth.

🔹 Family planning → helps reduce fertility and population growth rates.

⭐ Difference → Malthus emphasized natural and social checks, while Neo-Malthusians emphasize modern birth-control methods.

title: 🌱 4.1.3 BOSERUPIAN THEORY
notes:
Ester Boserup presented a contrasting view to Malthus.

🔹 Population growth → can stimulate agricultural innovation.

🔹 Increasing population pressure → encourages farmers to intensify production and develop new techniques.

🔹 Agricultural innovation → can increase food production.

⭐ Main idea → population pressure can become a stimulus for technological and agricultural development.

title: ⚒️ 4.1.4 MARXIAN PERSPECTIVE
notes:
Karl Marx rejected the idea that poverty is mainly caused by overpopulation.

🔹 Poverty → linked mainly to unequal distribution and control of resources.

🔹 Land, machinery and other productive resources → may be controlled by a small class.

🔹 Poor workers and peasants → may have limited access to means of subsistence.

🔹 Mechanization and changes in land ownership → can separate producers from their means of production.

⭐ Main idea → inequality and unequal access to resources are major causes of poverty.

title: 🔄 4.1.5 DEMOGRAPHIC TRANSITION THEORY
notes:
Demographic Transition Theory explains population change as societies develop economically and socially.

1️⃣ Stage 1 → high birth rate + high death rate → slow population growth.

2️⃣ Stage 2 → death rate falls while birth rate remains high → rapid population growth.

3️⃣ Stage 3 → birth rate declines → population growth slows.

4️⃣ Stage 4 → low birth rate + low death rate → stable or slowly growing population.

⭐ Development generally shifts populations from high mortality and fertility toward lower mortality and fertility.

title: 🏛️ 4.2 POPULATION POLICIES
notes:
Population policy → government policy designed to influence population growth, distribution and structure according to a country's economic, social, cultural, political and demographic conditions.

Two major categories:

🔴 Anti-natalist → aims to reduce fertility and population growth.

🟢 Pro-natalist → aims to increase fertility and population growth.

title: 👶 4.2.1 PRO-NATALIST POLICIES
notes:
Pro-natalist policies encourage people to have more children.

Possible measures →
🔹 Financial benefits for families.
🔹 Birth allowances or bonuses.
🔹 Tax incentives.
🔹 Maternity and parental benefits.
🔹 Child-care support.
🔹 Housing assistance.
🔹 Family-friendly employment policies.

⭐ Main purpose → increase fertility and population growth, especially where birth rates are low.

title: 🚼 4.2.2 ANTI-NATALIST POLICIES
notes:
Anti-natalist policies aim to reduce fertility and population growth.

Major approaches →
🔹 Family planning.
🔹 Access to contraception.
🔹 Reproductive-health services.
🔹 Public education and awareness.
🔹 Incentives or regulations intended to reduce large-family size.

🇨🇳 China → well-known example of an anti-natalist approach through its former one-child policy.

title: 🛑 4.3 MEASURES TO CURB POPULATION GROWTH
notes:
Population growth can be reduced through voluntary and policy-based measures.

🔹 Family planning programs.
🔹 Contraceptive access.
🔹 Reproductive-health education.
🔹 Delayed marriage and childbearing.
🔹 Female education.
🔹 Improved employment and economic opportunities for women.
🔹 Improved health services.
🔹 Reduction of infant and child mortality.

⭐ Effective population programs depend on accessibility, awareness, cultural acceptance and quality of services.

title: 🌍 4.3.1 INTERNATIONAL POPULATION MOVEMENTS
notes:
International concern over rapid population growth encouraged population conferences and family-planning initiatives.

📅 1974 → World Population Conference in Bucharest.

🔹 World Population Plan of Action → emphasized family planning, reducing rapid population growth, conserving resources and improving living standards.

⭐ International population programs focus on population growth, reproductive health, development and resource sustainability.

title: ⚠️ 4.3.2 CHALLENGES OF POPULATION CONTROL
notes:
Population-control programs can face several barriers:

🔹 Limited health facilities and equipment.
🔹 Lack of awareness.
🔹 Language barriers.
🔹 Limited accessibility of family-planning services.
🔹 Effectiveness and availability of methods.
🔹 Cultural acceptance.
🔹 Religious acceptance.
🔹 Acceptance by women and men.

⭐ Successful programs require accessible services, accurate information and community participation.

title: 💰 4.4 POPULATION & SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Population and development influence each other.

👥 Population growth can:
🔹 Increase the labor force.
🔹 Expand markets and demand.
🔹 Increase pressure on food, land, water and services.
🔹 Increase government demand for schools, housing and health facilities.

🌱 Development can:
🔹 Improve health and education.
🔹 Reduce mortality.
🔹 Change fertility patterns.
🔹 Improve living standards.

⭐ The effect of population growth depends on resources, technology, employment, institutions and the level of development.

title: 📊 4.4.1 CONCEPT OF DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Development → a process through which people and institutions improve their capacity to manage resources and achieve sustainable improvements in quality of life.

Major objectives:

1️⃣ Increase availability and distribution of basic necessities → food, shelter and health services.

2️⃣ Raise living standards → income, employment, education and cultural well-being.

3️⃣ Expand economic and social choices available to people.

⭐ Development is broader than economic growth alone.

title: 📏 4.4.2 INDICATORS OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Economic indicators measure the performance and strength of an economy.

🔹 GDP/GNP per capita → economic output or income per person.

🔹 GDP growth rate → rate at which total economic output changes.

🔹 Sectoral growth → growth of agriculture, industry, services and other sectors.

⭐ Per-capita measures help compare economic conditions between countries with different population sizes.

title: 👨‍👩‍👧 4.4.3 SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT INDICATORS
notes:
Social indicators measure people's social conditions and opportunities.

🔹 Social capital and institutions.
🔹 Discrimination.
🔹 Social exclusion.
🔹 Male and female literacy.
🔹 Girls-to-boys enrollment ratio.
🔹 Population below the poverty line.
🔹 Access to sanitation.

⭐ Social development focuses on people's well-being and participation in society.

title: 🏥 4.4.4 HEALTH & DEMOGRAPHIC INDICATORS
notes:
Important health and demographic indicators include:

🔹 Life expectancy at birth → expected average years of life.

🔹 Infant mortality rate → deaths of infants during the first year of life.

🔹 Child mortality rate → deaths among children within the specified early-childhood age group.

🔹 Maternal mortality ratio → maternal deaths associated with pregnancy and childbirth.

🔹 Percentage of underweight children → indicator of nutritional condition.

⭐ Health indicators help evaluate population well-being and development.

title: 🌱 4.4.5 FACTORS OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Development depends on several interacting factors.

🌍 Natural resources → provide materials and opportunities for production.

👨‍🏫 Human resources → education, skills, health and productivity of people.

💰 Capital → investment in infrastructure, machinery and productive activities.

⚙️ Technology → improves productivity and resource use.

🏛️ Institutions → effective governance and policies support development.

⭐ Sustainable development requires productive people, resources, technology, investment and effective institutions.

title: 🌍 4.5 POPULATION & ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH
notes:
Population growth, human activities and environmental conditions are closely connected.

Rapid population growth and poorly managed urbanization can increase pressure on:

💧 Water
🌳 Forests
🌾 Land
🌬️ Air quality
🗑️ Waste-management systems
🏠 Housing

⭐ Environmental degradation can directly and indirectly affect human health.

title: 💨 4.5.1 ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS
notes:
Major environmental-health concerns include:

🔹 Air pollution.
🔹 Unsafe water.
🔹 Poor sanitation and hygiene.
🔹 Food safety.
🔹 Hazardous materials.
🔹 Poor housing conditions.
🔹 Degraded ecosystems.
🔹 Workplace hazards.

⭐ Clean air, safe water, sanitation, healthy ecosystems and safe living conditions improve human health and productivity.

title: 🦠 4.5.2 ENVIRONMENT & DISEASE
notes:
Environmental conditions influence the emergence and spread of diseases.

🔹 Poor sanitation → increases water- and sanitation-related diseases.
🔹 Ecosystem degradation → can increase exposure to environmental hazards.
🔹 Biodiversity loss and disturbed ecosystems → can contribute to conditions favorable for emerging zoonotic diseases.
🔹 Poor air quality → increases respiratory and other health risks.

Examples of emerging/re-emerging diseases → COVID-19, Zika, Ebola, MERS, SARS and Marburg.

title: 🌿 4.5.3 ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP & PUBLIC HEALTH
notes:
Environmental stewardship → responsible management and protection of the environment to support human and ecosystem health.

Important actions →
🔹 Reduce unnecessary resource use.
🔹 Promote efficient production and consumption.
🔹 Protect and restore ecosystems.
🔹 Strengthen wetlands, watersheds and vegetation.
🔹 Promote sustainable farming.
🔹 Reduce excessive livestock and logging pressure.
🔹 Improve water, sanitation and hygiene.

⭐ Healthy ecosystems support healthy communities.

title: 🧠 UNIT 4 KEY DIFFERENCES
notes:
📈 Malthusian → population grows faster than food production.

🌱 Boserupian → population pressure can stimulate agricultural innovation.

⚒️ Marxian → poverty is strongly related to unequal resource access and distribution.

🔄 Demographic Transition → development is associated with changes from high birth/death rates to low birth/death rates.

🟢 Pro-natalist → increases fertility.

🔴 Anti-natalist → decreases fertility.

💰 Economic indicators → GDP/GNP per capita + economic growth + sectoral growth.

👥 Social indicators → literacy + enrollment + poverty + discrimination + exclusion + sanitation.

🏥 Health indicators → life expectancy + infant mortality + child mortality + maternal mortality + child nutrition.

🌿 Environmental health → links environmental quality with human health.
